subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Releasing reaction
hotspots.description: The burning log is an exothermic reaction — the wood's reactants release energy as heat and flame.
hotspots.positionHint: The campfire with its flame in the center.
hotspots.function: Shows a reaction releasing energy as fire.

hotspots.label: Energy escaping outward
hotspots.description: When the energy-out layer is on, glowing waves stream from the reaction into the surroundings — the released heat and light.
hotspots.positionHint: The radiating glow waves leaving the fire.
hotspots.function: Shows energy flowing out to the surroundings.

hotspots.label: Energy drop
hotspots.description: The energy-levels layer shows the reactants' energy high and the products' low — the difference between them is what the reaction releases.
hotspots.positionHint: The tall and short energy bars with the gap between them.
hotspots.function: Shows the energy drop from reactants to products.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A small stylized campfire floats centered, lit with soft neutral studio light — no bloom, no emissive in the asset itself (the flame glow is app-runtime). Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Log: soft warm-brown rounded cylinder; flame: soft amber/teal stylized shape; sparks: small teal dots. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots (coral / amber / molecular-green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Log: soft warm-brown matte, roughness ~0.6. Flame shape: soft translucent amber, alpha ~0.5, roughness ~0.5. Sparks: small teal dots. No emissive channels anywhere — the flame glow and energy waves are app runtime effects, not baked in.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a campfire as an exothermic reaction, built to be read as 'the reaction releases energy into its surroundings.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a small stylized campfire — one soft warm-brown rounded log (cylinder, radius ~0.45, length ~1.4) lying at center, a soft translucent amber flame shape (a few layered teardrop cones, alpha ~0.5) rising from it, and a few small teal spark dots floating up. Reactant molecule glyphs (app-rendered) hover faintly above.

2) ENERGY OUT (toggleable layer): soft concentric glow rings and wave arcs radiate outward from the flame (app-rendered), with small teal spark dots streaming outward — the released heat and light made visible.

3) ENERGY LEVELS (toggleable layer): two simple energy bars float beside the scene (app-rendered) — a TALL warm-orange bar labeled 'reactants' and a SHORT cool-gray bar labeled 'products,' with a soft glow band between them showing the released difference.

Camera: framed so the fire fills the center with negative space; auto-rotate default. Budget 5-9k triangles. Named nodes: FireLog, FlameCore, FlameLayers, Sparks, ReactantGlyphs, EnergyWaves, ReactantBar, ProductBar, ReleasedBand. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
